to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for selling and using paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant chooses a resource and its terms. A buyer approves a specific request, controls its wallet and spending, and receives the complete result in its existing application. The software connects that agreement to native settlement, delivery, fulfillment and recovery, so another engineer can take over the working service.

We request USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The funded outcome is two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators, and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators. Delivery progresses from installed customer services to recurring testnet use, mainnet use and an independent maintainer’s recovery and handover.

The existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration and complete-result receiving. The funded engineering extends that shared product through two independently operated deployments. T1 produces the source/runtime adapter changes, typed receiving mappings and authority-change handling required by the selected services. T2 adds the reusable registration and payment-policy compatibility needed to operate the same service through both facilitators, together with deployed monitoring and delivery-recovery changes. T3 delivers the production deployment, release/rollback and restoration improvements needed for maintainable mainnet installations. The resulting reusable code, deployment definitions and operating contracts return to the public product. Each installation provides a real source, useful customer task and independent receiving operator against which those improvements must work. Completed pre-award capabilities remain the starting product; the six packages below fund remaining prospective implementation.

Customer problem, need and adoption

A paid endpoint is useful when its output completes a customer’s task. An analyst may need every page of a dataset, the full filing comparison or a newly reviewed reporting period. An agent application may need a query result in its existing typed client. A merchant also needs to know which approved request was paid, what was delivered and whether the required order or accounting action finished.

Those jobs join four records: the approved request, settled transfer, complete output and accepted fulfillment or accounting. A task may require several priced requests, so the buyer needs its aggregate cost and complete output together. Staff must also recover an interrupted request and transfer the installed service to another maintainer.

Each selected installation uses an original workorder naming the payer, merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It also identifies the reason for a later purchase: a fresh period, changed source edition or distinct customer request. The same task then proceeds through installation, native payment, complete receiving, recurring use and handover.

The existing commercial model supports this adoption path: fixed-fee implementation of an agreed customer operation, followed by separately scoped care. A customer commissions the source and application adaptation; the merchant retains its resource receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. Actual acceptance, implementation effort, corrections, support demand and collections inform following offers.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar settles the operation the buyer approved. The approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers retain signing and aggregate spending authority. Merchants retain control of their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

Business value and adoption. The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

Technical improvement to be delivered. The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

Open Track scope. We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed Open Track fit.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the same useful service with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

StageImplemented behavior
Review and publishThe merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.
Connect the sourceAdapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.
Approve and purchaseThe buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.
Settle and deliverThe facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.
Use and continueThe receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.
Operate and hand overThe customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.

Recurring editorial data products. The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. Merged implementation and complete operating guide.

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow.

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. The receiving engineer can reopen the complete workspace, customer files and financial history and continue the same task.

Each connects its original transaction to the complete output. The funded milestones apply this working foundation to independent merchant and buyer operators.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are part of the 50-hour/$4,750 deployed-response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service: an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Their records retain the actual notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. An uncertain payment is reconciled through its original intent. A coverage gap remains visible until observation resumes.

A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. Original cohort operator guide.

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. This makes the funded targets assessable against the whole observation window.

For each installation, we record the customer’s existing task and, where available, its prior active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. Comparison uses the same input/output definition and source population or period. For the merchant's pricing work, we also record the active effort needed to reconcile usage, review the current price and prepare the next customer quote. The saved comparison retains its quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage; collections come from the original payment and accounting records. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany the measurements. The practical value is usable output, less manual work, recurring demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

The four SCF payments would be $3,800 at award acceptance, followed by $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective milestone approvals. These payments differ from the costs of completing each tranche. The request is denominated in USD-equivalent value and paid in XLM. Under SCF’s Official Rules §5.6, the XLM quantity uses CF XLMUSD_RR, or SDF’s selected qualifying alternative, reported on the day the award payment is made.

The complete resource study retains all six packages, their dependencies,400 hours and $38,000. With an illustrative December 7, 2026 start and its explicit working-day calendar, 25 engineering plus eight integration/handover hours per week is the lowest examined timely allocation. T1 finishes January 6 and final handover April 13, ahead of the illustrative May 6 day-150 target. The awarded schedule will use the actual acceptance date, named contributors and their working availability.

Under the selected schedule’s labor-accrual assumptions, the modeled peak additional cash requirement is $17,250 with a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days. Opening cash is currently unentered, and this application records no committed cash bridge or contributor payment deferral. Actual contributor payment dates, commitments, agreed deferrals and received funds belong in the original operating case. The forecast shows the amount those arrangements would need to cover; it does not establish that financing is available. Proposed commercial workshares retain their own assignments, stages and collections, and are not treated as received grant financing.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding tranche payment date. The actual payment record determines that form deadline; the 150-day delivery plan begins at award acceptance. For an anticipated delay, we will send written notice and obtain SDF’s written acknowledgment before the original deadline. A revised deadline will use SDF’s written confirmation. The grant case retains the deliverables, submissions, payments and this correspondence together, following Official Rules §5.8.

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source installation and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation, and separately scoped care. The original commercial workorder records delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Grant-funded reusable Stellar work and separately commissioned integration are assigned once. Additional reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining grant estimate.

Applicant, experience and submission
